annotations.title: CSV preflight: find what will break the import

description: Check a CSV before it is imported. Reports ragged rows, duplicate and empty column names, blank and duplicate rows, per-column type drift and column profiles, each with the row number a spreadsheet would show. Choose this when you have a CSV file and want the problems listed with the row numbers a spreadsheet shows: ragged rows, duplicate or empty column names, blank and duplicate rows, and per-column type drift. Do not choose this when you want the file fixed rather than diagnosed (use csv-clean), when you want a module that validates records in your own pipeline (use data-validation-module), or for a binary workbook such as xlsx, which this service cannot read. Example requests: Check this CSV for problems before I import it into Postgres. | Why does my CSV import fail? Here is the file. | Preflight a customer data export and tell me which rows are malformed.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

content.description: The customer's input.csv, as text. Supported: CSV, TSV or any delimiter-separated text (comma, semicolon, tab, pipe). Maximum 1048576 bytes.

inputs.title: CSV preflight: find what will break the import

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_csv_preflight

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.
